name: Tessera Neural Interdict Rifle NIR-2 'Migraine'
description:
A precision weapon that fires a focused electromagnetic pulse shaped into a narrow beam, designed to disrupt neural implants and BCI systems at range. The NIR-2 does not fire a physical projectile — it delivers a shaped EMP pulse through a directional antenna disguised as a rifle barrel.

The Migraine's beam induces cascading failures in neural interface hardware, causing effects ranging from disorientation and seizures to permanent implant damage depending on exposure duration and target's augmentation level. Against unaugmented targets, the weapon produces a splitting headache and temporary cognitive impairment. Against someone running a full BCI suite, it can cause a neural crash that leaves them unconscious for hours.

Tessera developed the NIR-2 for non-lethal interdiction scenarios — disabling augmented targets without the collateral damage of kinetic weapons. In practice, the line between 'disabled' and 'brain-damaged' has proven difficult to control.
specifications:
caliber: N/A — shaped EMP beam
effective_range: 50-500 meters
rate_of_fire: 1 pulse per 8 seconds
capacity: 12 pulses per power cell
weight: 6.2 kg
power_source: Dedicated EMP power cell, field-replaceable
tactical_use: The Migraine is deployed against augmented targets that need to be neutralized without kinetic engagement — hostage situations involving augmented hostage-takers, corporate espionage targets carrying sensitive neural data, and augmented individuals who might trigger deadman switches if killed. The weapon's non-lethal classification allows its use in scenarios where lethal force authorization has not been granted, though its potential for permanent brain damage makes that classification increasingly controversial.
cultural_context: The NIR-2 has become a flashpoint in debates about augmented rights in GLMZ. Disability advocates argue that a weapon specifically designed to attack neural implants constitutes targeted violence against augmented individuals. Tessera's defense — that the weapon is non-lethal and discriminate — rings hollow to anyone who has witnessed a neural crash firsthand. Underground augmentation communities have begun developing EMP-hardened implants specifically in response to the Migraine threat.
story_hooks: A modified NIR-2 was used in a crowded transit station, inducing neural crashes in every augmented person within a 50-meter radius. The weapon was supposed to be focused on a single target. Either it was modified for area effect, or the operator deliberately chose to attack a crowd.
A Tessera whistleblower has leaked documents showing that the NIR-2 was originally developed as a lethal weapon — the 'non-lethal' designation was a marketing decision, not an engineering one.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular sniper platform that resembles a precision rifle at first glance, but with an unsettling asymmetry — the barrel is thinner than expected and wrapped in a mesh antenna grid rather than traditional rifling. The overall silhouette is predatory and minimalist, all sharp lines and purposeful geometry. There's an uncanny quality to it; it looks like a weapon designed to wound consciousness itself rather than flesh.
physical_description.dimensions: Length: 118 cm | Barrel (antenna assembly): 61 cm | Width at stock: 8 cm | Height (with scope rail): 14 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light at 6.2 kg — noticeably lighter than kinetic sniper rifles of similar length. Feels almost hollow when shouldered, with weight distributed toward the receiver rather than the barrel, making it bottom-heavy and easy to aim but vaguely unsettling to handle.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite (graphene-infused polycarbonate) with aluminum alloy spine and titanium heat-dissipation fins around the power cell housing
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal gray with brushed titanium accents. The antenna barrel shows a subtle iridescent sheen under certain angles — the mesh weave catches light like oil on water. Heavy weathering and micro-scarring typical of field use; some units show scorch marks from thermal bleed-off.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: flat gunmetal gray | Accents: brushed titanium, faint electric blue traces along the antenna mesh | Power cell indicator: soft amber/red LED
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip with aggressive stippling for secure handling even in wet conditions. The stock features wrapped aramid cord padding — functional and tactile, designed to absorb minor impacts.
distinctive_features: Antenna barrel grid: visible mesh weave instead of traditional rifling, almost translucent in certain lighting
Capacitor nodes: three small cylindrical protrusions along the receiver spine, each with a faint blue indicator LED
Heat vents: narrow slits along the barrel shroud, occasionally showing thermal residue from recent discharge
Non-standard scope rail: reinforced titanium attachment point, slightly offset to compensate for antenna asymmetry
Power cell magazine: transparent polymer housing revealing the dense crystalline core of the EMP cell, glowing soft amber when charged
Charging contacts: exposed copper contact points on the rear of the power cell magazine, darker with oxidation on well-used units
Arcing scars: subtle burn marks around the antenna aperture from previous pulse discharges — permanent aesthetic damage that marks heavy use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Perfect Recall Storage serial plate: brushed aluminum, mounted on the left side of the receiver just above the grip. Markings are small and utilitarian. 'TESSERA NIR-2' stamped in block letters on the barrel shroud. Proprietary microdot security serial on the power cell housing, only visible under UV light.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but visibly used. Field weapons show consistent thermal scarring, minor polymer stress fractures, and oxidized charging contacts. Military/corporate units are meticulously maintained; black-market variants show obvious jury-rigging — mismatched power cells, tape reinforcements, and crude modifications to capacitor nodes.
